about: The shipped playbook with "bounce_lands": true on its cast block (harness 0.4.16): a land that returns a land is played late in the turn, and also when Forge's AI would hold it for want of a basic land. For the seats that sit on two or three lands with such a land in hand (DESIGN.md section 46).

when: not controls Chulane, Teller of Tales

playbook.notes: Deep Clue Sea (Morska, Undersea Sleuth: a Clue every upkeep, two +1/+1 counters whenever the second card of a turn is drawn, no maximum hand size). What stock Forge leaves undone (12 audit games, seeds 3101-3112): Morska comes down on turn 7.0; of 176 Clues it cracks 32, every one on another player's turn, so her counters arrive three times a game; Krosan Verge sits unused for 20 turns; the four cards flagged AI:RemoveDeck:All are never cast (Selvala, Jolrael, Psychosis Crawler, Esix); and it casts Farewell on its own board (1 of the 12, 6 of 20 tuning games, 12 of 40 validation games). The rules: Sol Ring and, to turn 5, the two-mana rocks, then Morska; Krosan Verge fetched while there are seven lands or fewer; Mechanized Production only on a Clue (eight Clues win the game), and no Clue sacrificed while it or Tangletrove Kelp (Clues attack as 6/6) is out, whether by cracking or by Sophia; Selvala and Idol of Oblivion tapped for the turn's second card; the cards that pay for that second card first (Kelp, Selvala, Idol, Jolrael, Detective of the Month, Alandra, Ethereal Investigator, Tezzeret, Knowledge Is Power, Chulane, Thought Monitor), then one Clue cracked a turn when nothing else has drawn it (not with Bennie Bracks or Chulane out, who draw it anyway; a second rule after the casts catches the turn they do not); Jolrael's X/X before an attack of four or more with seven cards in hand; further Clues cracked before combat under Knowledge Is Power, with Psychosis Crawler out, or on a hand of two or fewer; every other permanent in a fixed order, rocks and On the Trail last after turn 5; Bennie Bracks only when there is no attacker for his convoke to tap (cast by rule in the first main phase he tapped Morska and cost two attacks in the first twelve games); Hydroid Krasis for four or more, Finale of Revelation on a short hand. Kept from Forge: Farewell unless an opponent's creatures out-power ours; Lonis's reveal, which sacrifices every Clue the seat has; Tezzeret's emblem, which decked the seat (seed 3121, stock and one variant); Esix is named by no rule, since Forge's AI answers its replacement by copying Morska, a copy that dies to the legend rule in place of the upkeep Clue. Triggers: Nadir Kraken's {1} always, Killer Service's Rhino when there is a Food to give up. Attack: go-wide at the highest life with the split. Library guards (20, 30 for Finale) on every rule that draws. Goldfish, seeds not looked at before the rules were final (3201-3240, 40 games a side, every game finished): stock 12.57 turns, this file 9.70, 2.88 turns faster (95% +2.24 to +3.51; faster in 36, same in 3, slower in 1). On the 28 seeds where stock did not cast Farewell the difference is 1.93 turns (95% +1.42 to +2.44); 7 of the 40 games under the rules end with Mechanized Production (stock: 5). On the seeds the rules were written on (3101-3112, 3121-3140) it is 2.58 turns over the 31 of 32 that stock finishes. Cracking the Clue only after the casts instead of before them changes nothing in goldfish (0.03 turns on the 31 of those seeds both versions finish). Not played at tables yet. What goldfish cannot price: Selvala's parley hands each opponent a card a turn, Lonis's steals are given up, and a tall Morska has no evasion. Shipped on 2026-11-12 as version 1 with the attack left to Forge: at 200 tables of bots (ab-run #19 and #23, seed 20261210) 76 wins against the stock pilot's 52 (+12.0 points, 95% +4 to +20, exact test 0.0071); 61 with the go-wide attack these rules were written with. Version 2 (candidate `answers`, 2026-11-13): answer rules, every shipped rule kept in its order. Written from the 600 games of league-run #3 (seed 20261250, Deep Clue Sea in 200, 74 wins): the three wipes were drawn in 63 (Farewell), 72 (Fumigate) and 63 (Organic Extinction) games and cast in 6, 5 and 4; each sat in hand for about 380 of the seat's own turns and was in hand at 9 to 11 of its losses; most losses came from a wide token board (Zombie, Goblin, Soldier, Shark, Plant tokens dealing 40 to 96 of the damage). Reconstructing creature counts from the zone events, on the seat's own turns with a wipe in hand and five lands or more: when the widest opponent had 8 to 12 creatures and more than the seat, the seat died within two turn cycles in 30 to 37% of those turns (17 of 57, 18 of 49) and won 28 of 57 and 17 of 49; with 13 or more and behind, 36 of 96 and 34 won; at 4 to 7 opposing creatures it was about 24%, and when the seat had at least as many creatures as the widest opponent it almost never died that soon at 8 or more (1 of 31 turns). Our life under 20 with an opponent at six creatures or more: 54 of 92 such turns ended in death within two cycles. Rules 1-3, Organic Extinction (destroys nonartifact creatures only, so our Clues, rocks, Tangletrove Kelp, Thought Monitor, Psychosis Crawler, Kappa Cannoneer and Academy Manufactor stay; improvise lets the Clues pay): an opponent with 8 creatures and more than ours; or one opponent's attack next turn (threat) at or above our life; or our life at 20 or less, an opponent with 6 creatures and more power than ours. Rules 4-6, Fumigate (all creatures, a life a creature): the same three, the count rule not while Tangletrove Kelp is out (it would die and the Clues stop being 6/6 attackers) and the threat rule only when an opponent out-powers us. Rules 7-8, Farewell (modes are chosen by Forge as it is cast: in the league and locally it exiled our Clues and rocks along with the creatures, 16 of our tokens in one local cast): only at 10 opposing creatures, more than ours and more power, with neither Mechanized Production (it would exile the aura's artifacts) nor Tangletrove Kelp out; or at threat >= life with more opposing power whatever is out (a first version kept Mechanized Production out of this rule too, and a local seat with it and six Clues out held Farewell at 18 life and died that turn cycle to nine 4/4 flying Angels); the shipped hold on Farewell stays below them. These sit above every engine rule, so the wipe comes before the turn's creatures. Rule 14, Aerial Extortionist above Morska: its entry exiles a nonland permanent (Forge picks; every league cast took an opponent's) and the shipped list cast it in 17 of the 60 games it was drawn, held for 267 own turns, often at six lands or more while the turn's mana went to recasting Morska at a growing commander tax; cast first whenever an opponent has 8 power or more. Left to Forge: Swords to Plowshares (53 of 54 games) and Disorder in the Court (50 of 51), which Forge casts and aims; Confirm Suspicions (12 of 58, in hand at 9 losses), a counterspell, out of the rules' reach; Junk Winder and Koma stay in the shipped list. Local tables of bots (16 games, seeds 20263010-20263012, opponents under their shipped playbooks; too few games to measure anything, 7 wins): Fumigate seen in 7 games and cast in 5, Organic Extinction 7 and 3 (improvise paid it at five to seven lands), Farewell 5 and 1 (in two of the others the seat never reached six lands), Aerial Extortionist 5 and 5 (before it moved above Morska it sat in hand at 8 to 13 lands for six turns while each turn's mana recast Morska). The wipes took 10 to 27 opposing permanents for 0 to 8 of ours each; the one Farewell took 20 of theirs and 19 of ours (16 of them Clues). Which rule fired is not in the logs (playbook_stats are summed over the table's playbook seats); the one Farewell cast came at ten or more opposing creatures, so by rule 7. A candidate: not played at 200 tables. Shipped as version 2 on 2026-11-14 from ab-run #33: on the same 200 tables of bots (seed 20261300, opponents drawn from the other eleven bots under their playbooks of 2026-11-13) it won 71 against version 1's 67 (+2.0 points, 95% -3 to +7, exact test 0.57); the cards the new rules name were cast in 97 of the 161 games they were drawn, under version 1 in 4 of 157. It has not been set against its stock pilot. What it still casts in a share of games 15 points or more below stock AI's (the stock arm of ab-run #26, other tables of the same pool), 22 cards: Graf Mole, Wilderness Reclamation, Search the Premises, Merchant of Truth, Innocuous Researcher, Magnifying Glass and 16 more (demo-data/playtest/2026-11-14/pool-answers/deep-clue-sea-check.txt). VERSION 3 CANDIDATE `hooksopen` (2026-11-21). Version 2 with five changes: after Forge's own attack has been declared, the attackers sent at a player are sent at the opponent that looks most dangerous instead, when that opponent is ahead of the one attacked by five or more and the attack is no worse there: the damage sure to get through whatever is blocked is at least what it was, no more creatures there could block the attackers, and no attacker meets a blocker that would destroy it unless it met one where it was sent (`"aim": "danger"`; an attack that is sure to kill its target stays, and which creatures attack is not changed); and then the creatures that stayed home attack an opponent that has no creature that can block, the most dangerous such opponent first: those that deal damage, have no ability that taps them (or have vigilance) and are not wanted home by Forge's own judgement of the seat's defence (`"open": true`; a weaker opponent is not killed this way while a more dangerous one lives); and then a sure kill is taken from the most dangerous opponent down (`"finish": "leader"`: enough attackers are put on the opponent that looks most dangerous that the damage reaches its life whatever it blocks, then on the next one, and no weaker opponent is killed while a more dangerous one lives); and then a triggered ability of the seat that removes one permanent of an opponent (destroys it, exiles it, returns it to hand or library) is aimed at the opponent that looks most dangerous, when that opponent looks more dangerous than the one Forge aimed at by five or more and has a permanent of the same kind worth at least as much as Forge's choice or at least 4 (`"targets": {"triggers": "danger"}`); and then when Forge's blocks leave at least the seat's life in damage unblocked and blocks exist that would not, blocks are added, the least valuable free creatures in front of the heaviest unblocked attackers and only as many as it takes for the seat to live (`"block": {"survive": true}`). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 3: the `hooksopen` arm of ab-run #59 (seed 20261400, the tables of ab-run #58; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v27/, DESIGN.md section 38). Beside version 2 on the same 200 tables of the pool: 65 wins against 54 (27 tables against 16, exact test 0.13); the `hooks` arm 64. Free damage is in because the arm with it won more of these tables than the arm without: the better of two on the tables that measured it; its confirming run on tables that chose nothing is still to be played (after ab-run #62, the exam of the five pool decks that got no hook). VERSION 4 CANDIDATE `guard`. Version 3 with one change: after Forge's own attack has been declared and the hooks the version already has have acted, attackers are taken back when the attack leaves the seat where the opponents one after another are sure to kill it before its next turn and keeping them home prevents that, or, when nothing kept home does, where one opponent alone is (`"guard": "table"`; a sure kill's attackers stay, and an attack stands when nothing kept home would save the seat). No cast or trigger rule is changed. SHIPPED 2026-11-22 as version 4: the `guard` arm of ab-run #63 (seed 20261450, tables that chose nothing; demo-data/ab/2026-11-22-ab-v31/, DESIGN.md section 40). On the same 200 tables of the pool: versions 2, 3 and 4 won 58, 58 and 60; version 3 beside 2 20 tables against 20 (exact test 1.00), version 4 beside 3 6 against 4 (exact test 0.75); dead with its own creatures tapped 20, 13 and 12 times. Read over the seven decks together by the rules fixed before the run: the versions with the hooks stand (139 tables against 142) and the guard holds (27 against 29; out before its next turn on 18 of the 175 tables its attack changed first, from 31). CANDIDATE lands (2026-11-23, harness 0.4.16): "bounce_lands": true on the cast block. Forge's script lets its AI play a land that returns a land (Gruul Turf and its kind) only while it controls a basic land, so a seat whose lands are all nonbasic holds it for the rest of the game; and when the AI does play one it plays it first thing in its turn and returns an untapped land. With the key such a land is played after the rules have spent the turn's mana, and at the end of the second main phase when Forge's AI would not play it at all, and it returns a tapped land before an untapped one and a basic before a nonbasic.
